messages.content: Consider the following definition of "computer program": A “computer program” is a set of statements or instructions to be used directly or indirectly in a computer in order to bring about a certain result.   Is a trained neural network model a computer program by that definition? Ensure that the ratio of sentence types (declarative, interrogative, exclamatory) in your response is balanced.

message.content:
A trained neural network model can be treated as a computer program when its weights and architecture guide a computer toward a specified result.
The model may act as indirect instructions because an interpreter executes operations based on the learned parameters.
The strongest answer depends on whether the term includes learned data used as executable control.
Does the model itself contain statements or instructions?
Does the computer use those parameters directly or indirectly to bring about a result?
Would a legal or technical context accept the broad definition?
The answer is nuanced!
The model-and-interpreter pair is persuasive!
The plain weights alone are less certain!
